CELL WALL LAYERED STRUCTURE
                          
   Middle Lamella (Ca/Mg Pectate) ──► Primary Wall ──► Secondary Wall (S₁, S₂, S₃) ──► Plasma Membrane
conceptBreakdown.content:
The plant cell wall is a rigid, non-living extracellular exoskeleton providing tensile support and osmotic protection.

### Cell Wall Layers
1. **Middle Lamella**: Outermost cementing layer between adjacent plant cells composed of **Calcium and Magnesium Pectates**. During fruit ripening, pectinase enzymes dissolve pectates, softening the fruit.
2. **Primary Cell Wall**: Thin ($1\text{--}3\ \mu\text{m}$), flexible, extensible layer formed by young growing cells. Composed of cellulose microfibrils in a matrix of hemicellulose, pectin, and structural extensin proteins. Grows by **intussusception** (insertion of new wall material).
3. **Secondary Cell Wall**: Thick, rigid, non-extensible layer deposited inner to the primary wall after cell expansion ceases. Stratified into $S_1, S_2, S_3$ layers, heavily impregnated with **Lignin** (in sclerenchyma and xylem) or **Suberin** (in cork).

conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Plasmodesmata**: Microscopic membrane-lined cytoplasmic bridges traversing primary cell walls and middle lamellae, linking neighboring protoplasts into a continuous **Symplast**.
• **Desmotubule**: A central, tightly rolled cylindrical tubule traversing the plasmodesmatal pore, derived directly from the **Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER)**.
